game: Fresno State Bulldogs@San Diego State Aztecs

guide_enrichment.narrative:
We understand why the market is leaning heavily on Fresno State’s recent form. Fresno State has averaged 430 yards and 34.8 points during its four-game winning streak while committing only three turnovers and forcing 11. That is meaningful context, but our view is that the path to creating consistent scoring opportunities becomes more difficult against a San Diego State defense that rates substantially better in prevention than Fresno State does in creation.

The concern for us is the other side of the ball. Fresno State’s last four opponents combined for only four red-zone possessions, and its pass defense produced seven interceptions over that span. San Diego State’s passing profile is poorly positioned to attack that strength, so we are not building the case around a productive night from its offense.

For us, the wager is instead about the market asking Fresno State to create more separation than our overall matchup profile supports. San Diego State’s defense gives it a credible way to keep the game compressed, even if its offense has trouble sustaining drives. That defensive resistance is the main reason our expectation differs from the market.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch:
We will be watching Fresno State’s offense against San Diego State’s scoring-opportunity prevention. Jayden Mandal has gone 122 consecutive attempts without an interception, and Fresno State has protected him well enough to allow only two sacks during its winning streak. If Fresno State maintains that efficiency and repeatedly creates short-field scoring chances, San Diego State will struggle to stay within range.

Our numbers, however, point to a more demanding matchup than Fresno State’s recent production might suggest. We think San Diego State’s ability to limit quality possessions—not its ability to trade scores—is the most important part of the case.

recent_game.fact: Fresno State improved to 4-1 overall and 1-0 in Pac-12 play with a 26-6 road win over Washington State on October 3.
Fresno State held Washington State to 182 total yards, 30 rushing yards, nine first downs and no touchdowns; the Cougars averaged 2.7 yards per play and converted 3 of 13 third downs.
Fresno State possessed the ball for a season-high 35:59 at Washington State.
Fresno State recorded five sacks at Washington State.

quarterback.fact: Jayden Mandal is listed as Fresno State's starting quarterback, with Khristian Martin as the backup.
Mandal has completed 91 of 137 passes for 1,034 yards, six touchdowns and one interception through five games.
During Fresno State's four-game winning streak, Mandal completed 84 of 122 passes for 957 yards and six touchdowns without an interception.
Mandal has attempted 122 consecutive passes without an interception and has added 128 rushing yards and one touchdown during the four-game winning streak.

offensive_personnel.fact: Fresno State's listed starting skill personnel are running back Rayshon Luke, receivers Josiah Freeman, Jahlil McClain and Ezekiel Avit, and tight end Jake Appleget.
Luke leads Fresno State with 286 rushing yards on 42 carries, while Bryson Donelson has 206 yards and four touchdowns on 48 carries.
Freeman has 25 receptions for 322 yards and two receiving touchdowns, and Avit has 13 catches for 234 yards and two touchdowns.
Luke and Donelson have combined for 492 rushing yards and five touchdowns on 90 carries, accounting for 64 percent of Fresno State's rushing production.

defensive_personnel.fact: Linebacker K'vion Thunderbird leads Fresno State with 39 tackles, 14 more than any other Bulldog.
Defensive lineman Dylan Hampsten leads Fresno State with 5.5 tackles for loss and 2.5 sacks and has recorded a tackle for loss in every game.
Simeon Harris has three interceptions, Ethan Tierney has two, and Kiontre Harris and Justin Johnson have one each.
Justin Johnson recorded his first career interception at Washington State and returned it 15 yards.

coaching_changes.fact: Fresno State is in its second season under head coach Matt Entz and retained its entire defensive staff for 2026.
Josh Davis is the offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach, Nick Benedetto is the defensive coordinator and safeties coach, and Brian Ferentz coaches the offensive line.
